questions.q: At which access step do heat-exposed informal-worker households lose the most potential support?
questions.have: Separate administrative stocks and a small commissioned facilitation assessment; no complete representative ladder.
questions.could: Voluntary repeated survey before, during and after a hot season, publishing only aggregate group and step results.
questions.scale: About 1,500 households across six districts; final size depends on detectable differences.

questions.q: Does receiving an existing transfer before peak heat improve coping compared with later receipt?
questions.have: Entitlements and heat earnings-loss evidence; little verified payment-timing evidence.
questions.could: Evaluate an authorised timing change with aggregate earnings, care costs and borrowing outcomes.
questions.scale: About 2,000 households across 40-60 clusters, subject to power analysis.

questions.q: How much of household heat-illness cost is met through PM-JAY and free public care?
questions.have: Hospital-cover rules and service policies; no verified heat-specific cost pathway.
questions.could: Consent-based care-cost study across public and empanelled facilities, publishing aggregate results.
questions.scale: About 600 episodes across 12 facilities in one season.

questions.q: Does assisted scheme navigation improve timely receipt during a hot season?
questions.have: Delivery models and commissioned assessment; no verified heat-specific causal estimate.
questions.could: Phased rollout of additional support against existing services, measuring receipt and timing; providers on equal terms.
questions.scale: About 60 communities and 1,800 households; subject to power analysis.

questions.q: Can public works cushion heat income loss while reducing exposure?
questions.have: Historical learning protection evidence; no verified 2026-framework heat evaluation.
questions.could: Evaluate adjusted hours, rest and water provision alongside work access and wage arrival.
questions.scale: About 50 worksites across four districts in one hot season.

questions.q: Is what a household receives from rural work, pensions or food rations enough to cover a hot season's lost earnings and care costs?
questions.have: Documents, applications, enrolment, receipt and payment timing are measured for some schemes, such as fund transfer orders for rural work. No source checked measures whether support is adequate in a hot season.
questions.could: Compare the support received with heat-season losses in the same households, in a hot month and a cooler one.
questions.scale: Illustrative: about 600 households in three districts

questions.q: How many informal workers exposed to heat know which schemes they could use, and how many of them qualify?
questions.have: Later steps are measured for some schemes; awareness and eligibility are not, in the sources checked.
questions.could: Pair a short awareness survey with an eligibility screen for the same workers, at worksites and markets.
questions.scale: Illustrative: about 800 workers in two cities

schemes.name: Viksit Bharat - Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin)
schemes.run_by: Ministry of Rural Development and state governments
schemes.who: Rural households whose adult members volunteer for unskilled manual work.
schemes.gives: 125 days of wage employment per financial year; wage rates vary.
schemes.delivery: Work on demand; wages through bank or post-office accounts.
schemes.documents: Existing job cards remain valid; the complete new application checklist was not verified.
schemes.speed: Published rule: weekly payment or within fifteen days of muster-roll closure; actual receipt times not verified.
schemes.heat_relevance: Could replace some lost rural earnings, depending on work availability, safe conditions and payment timing.
